title: Indian Wedding Outfits for Every Function: A 5-Event Checklist
excerpt: Plan Indian wedding outfits for every function, from haldi to reception, with a simple checklist, smart re-wear tricks and an ordering timeline.
body:
Planning outfits for a five-function Indian wedding is easier when you work backwards from the events: haldi, mehendi, sangeet, wedding ceremony and reception. Give each one a mood, a colour and a comfort level, then fill in the outfits, jewellery and shoes. Start four weeks out, and you will never be the guest frantically ironing at midnight.

## Step one: get the schedule and the themes

Before you buy anything, ask the family or check the invite for three things: the date and time of each function, the venue (indoor, lawn, poolside, temple), and any colour theme. Many families now set a theme, such as yellow for haldi, green for mehendi or pastels for a day wedding. A theme saves you a lot of guessing.

Write the functions in a list on your phone. Next to each, note whether it is day or night, indoors or outdoors, and how much you will be sitting, standing or dancing. That simple note will shape every choice that follows.

## The function-by-function checklist

| Function | Mood | Colours | Fabric and silhouette | Shoes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haldi | Playful, messy | Yellow, mustard, white | Washable cotton kurti or tunic with pants | Flat sandals |
| Mehendi | Relaxed, colourful | Green, pink, multicolour | Cotton or block print palazzo set | Flats or juttis |
| Sangeet | Party, dancing | Bright jewel tones | Light Anarkali or flared suit in chiffon or georgette | Cushioned juttis |
| Wedding ceremony | Traditional | Pink, peach, coral, gold | Chanderi, silk or embroidered suit with dupatta | Easy slip-ons |
| Reception | Glamorous | Emerald, wine, pastel with shine | Taffeta, organza or embellished Anarkali | Block heels |

## Outfit ideas for each event

**Haldi.** Turmeric stains, so wear something you are happy to wash. A simple embroidered top like the [Yellow Embroidered Cotton Tunic Top with Black Floral Yoke](/products/yellow-black-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) with white cotton pants hits the yellow theme without risking a precious outfit.

**Mehendi.** You will sit for a long time while henna dries, so choose loose, breathable pieces with sleeves you can push up. The [Sage Teal Hand Block Print Cotton Kurta Palazzo Set](/products/sage-teal-block-print-cotton-kurta-palazzo-set/) is comfortable on floor cushions and looks pretty in daylight photos.

**Sangeet.** This is the dancing night, so prioritise movement. An Anarkali with a light flare is ideal. The [Purple Bandhani Chiffon Anarkali Suit Set](/products/purple-bandhani-chiffon-anarkali-suit-set/) twirls beautifully and stays light through hours on the dance floor.

**Wedding ceremony.** The most traditional event and often the longest. Choose a respectful, elegant look with a dupatta for covering your head if needed. The [Coral Pink Chanderi Kurta Set with Hand-Embroidered Yoke](/products/coral-pink-chanderi-hand-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) has the soft sheen and modest cut that suits pheras and family photos.

**Reception.** Time for your most glamorous piece. A taffeta silk Anarkali such as the [Sage Green Taffeta Silk Gota Work Anarkali with Sequin Organza Dupatta](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) catches the evening lights and feels special.

## How to re-wear without anyone noticing

Five functions do not have to mean five brand new outfits. Some smart swaps:

- Wear the same kurta pant set to the haldi and the mehendi with a different dupatta and jewellery.
- Pair an Anarkali's dupatta with a plain kurta set to create a new look.
- Use one statement dupatta across two plain outfits.
- Change your hair: a braid with flowers for the mehendi, a sleek bun for the reception.

A good rule is two hero outfits (sangeet and reception), two mid-level outfits (ceremony and one day event) and one easy outfit for the haldi.

## Accessories and packing list

Beyond outfits, tick these off before the first function:

- Two or three pairs of earrings: small, medium and statement
- Bangles in neutral gold or silver that match everything
- Juttis plus one pair of block heels
- Safety pins, double-sided tape and a small sewing kit
- A shawl or jacket for cold evenings in north India
- A clutch big enough for your phone and lipstick

## Your ordering timeline

If you are buying new outfits, especially from abroad, timing is everything. Made-to-measure pieces take 5–7 working days to stitch plus about 5–10 business days for delivery. That is why you should order at least three to four weeks before the first function. It leaves time for a try-on and, if needed, a small alteration.

Ordering custom pieces also means each outfit fits on the first try. Read more about our [custom fit](/custom-stitched-indian-suits-made-to-measure/) service if you have a non-standard size or want a particular length.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many outfits do I need for a five-function wedding?**
Ideally five, but three or four is enough if you re-style with different dupattas, jewellery and hair.

**What should I wear to a haldi if I am not close family?**
Any bright, washable cotton outfit in yellow or white is perfect. Guests may also get turmeric applied, so skip delicate fabrics.

**Which function should get my best outfit?**
Usually the sangeet or reception, since these are the most glamorous and photographed evening events.

**When should I order outfits for a winter wedding?**
At least three to four weeks before the first function, and earlier in peak season between November and February.
